The key point is that, for a fixed \(M\), only finitely many “relevant Zeckendorf-prefix states” can occur when tracking the first \(M\) reversed digits under multiplication by \(q\). In fact, the underlying equivalence relation has at most \(3^M\) classes, and multiplication by \(q\) acts effectively on these classes.

So along the orbit
\[
u,\ uq,\ uq^2,\ uq^3,\dots,
\]
the associated state sequence must repeat within fewer than \(3^M\) steps. Once a state repeats, the future evolution is periodic, hence the membership pattern
\[
n\mapsto \mathbf 1_{u q^n\in \mathcal K_{\mathcal F}^{(M)}}
\]
is either eventually all false (finite case) or ultimately periodic. Because the state space and transition are effective, one can:

- compute such a preperiod and period,
- decide whether \(S_u^{(M)}\) is finite or infinite,
- and in the finite case list all elements.

Moreover, the repetition argument gives the explicit bounds
\[
n_0<3^M,\qquad 1\le p\le 3^M.
\]

That is exactly choice **(A)**.
